claim: When senescent cells accumulate, they may contribute to sagging skin, muscle weakness, and chronic conditions such as osteoarthritis and type 2 diabetes.
label: TRUE
annotatorNote: [AI label: Claude, 2026-10-02 - not yet checked by the human annotator] A hedged claim ('may contribute'), and that is what the literature says: senescent cells are implicated in osteoarthritis, metabolic dysfunction and type 2 diabetes, and physical dysfunction (Chaib, Tchkonia & Kirkland, Nat Med 2022), and in skin ageing incl. loss of elasticity and wrinkles (Chin et al., Front Physiol 2023).
